content: The deep cervical lymph nodes are a collection of lymph nodes located in close proximity to the internal jugular vein. These lymph nodes can be categorized into two primary groups: the upper group, also referred to as the superior group, and the lower group, also known as the inferior group. Another method of classification divides them into the deep anterior cervical lymph nodes and the deep lateral cervical lymph nodes. Additionally, they can be further subdivided into three distinct groups based on their anatomical position along the jugular vein: the superior deep jugular lymph nodes, the middle deep jugular lymph nodes, and the inferior deep jugular lymph nodes.
